subject: Biotechnology
title: Indigenous Data Sovereignty
description: A quick, practical guide to Indigenous Data Sovereignty.

hook.text: The Havasupai donated blood for diabetes research — scientists used it for schizophrenia and migration studies without consent.

buildup.text: Indigenous communities have been exploited by genetic research — samples taken without proper informed consent or benefit sharing.

discovery.text: The CARE Principles — Collective Benefit, Authority, Responsibility, Ethics — give indigenous peoples control over genomic data.

twist.text: Genetic ancestry tests can contradict indigenous oral histories — raising tensions between scientific and cultural narratives.

climax.text: The Global Indigenous Data Alliance advocates that indigenous peoples govern collection, ownership, and use of their data.

punchline.text: Their genes, their rules — data sovereignty protects indigenous communities in genomics.

quiz.question: What do the CARE Principles ensure for indigenous communities in genomics research?
options: Free access to all genetic databases worldwide
Community control over collection, ownership, and use of their genomic data
Automatic inclusion in all medical research studies

details.summary: Indigenous data sovereignty asserts that genetic and health data from indigenous communities should be controlled by those communities, not external researchers or corporations. Historical exploitation of indigenous genetic material without consent drives this movement.
details.whyItMatters: Indigenous peoples have been disproportionately subjected to genetic research without meaningful consent or benefit sharing. Data sovereignty frameworks protect communities from exploitation while enabling research partnerships built on trust.
takeaways: Indigenous communities assert governance over their genetic and health data
Historical exploitation without consent drives demand for data sovereignty
CARE principles complement FAIR data standards with indigenous governance

faq.question: What historical exploitation drives indigenous data sovereignty?
faq.answer: The Havasupai tribe's DNA collected for diabetes research was used without consent for studies on migration and mental illness. Similar cases worldwide prompted indigenous communities to demand control over their genetic data and require community-level consent.

faq.question: What are the CARE principles for indigenous data?
faq.answer: CARE stands for Collective benefit, Authority to control, Responsibility, and Ethics. They ensure indigenous communities benefit from research using their data, maintain governance authority, and that researchers uphold ethical obligations beyond standard informed consent.
